title: Finite state, and what breaks it
claim: T1: in the A79 language the self-holding definitions' relations at depth t form a deterministic sequence in at most 16^s values, so every relation and whether the depth-t pattern lives are eventually periodic (preperiod plus period at most 16^s); the bottomless pattern lives iff the main relation is non-empty at the greatest fixed point (at most 4s strict decreases from nothing; compactness); the usual limit is the bottomless pattern with the knot added on the ports of each self-holding definition with a pass-through call. T2: the states a depth-t pattern allows on any fixed top window are a function of the relations b levels down, so a top window reads depth only modulo the period. P3a: an inequality gadget of four knots on distinct distinctions, equality by two. P3b: every complement-closed relation is NAE-definable (Boehler et al. 2005 with P3a). P3c: for translation-invariant meeting patterns on Z^2, life is undecidable (the domino problem; Berger 1966; Freedman 1998).
failure_conditions: A description whose relation sequence is not eventually periodic within 16^s, or whose usual limit differs from the modified bottomless pattern.
A top-window state set at depth t not determined by the relations b levels down.
A failure of the gadget, of one of the 16 three-place definitions, or of the tile encoding on a finite torus.
foundation_claim_scope: Patterns of NAE knots on distinct distinctions: nested descriptions of the A79 language (T1, T2) and translation-invariant patterns on Z^2 (P3c); no source label claimed for infinite patterns.
